column1: Overall, the town changed significantly from a mostly empty rural area into a modern coastal town. The industrial zone and grasslands were completely replaced by residential buildings, recreational facilities, and new roads.
In 1950, Pentland had very basic infrastructure. A main road ran from the south to the sea in the north.
There was an industrial area on the western side and a car park on the eastern side, connected by two side paths.
Large areas of grassland covered the rest of the land in the west and east.
By 2007, the town had developed substantially. A marina was built in the sea, and a curved road was added along the coastline.
On the western side, the industrial area was replaced by a park, a swimming pool, and a multi-storey car park.
On the eastern side, the old car park and part of the grassland were removed to build several apartment blocks.
In the south, a new main road was built with shops on both sides.
Two rows of houses were constructed in the south-east, while a cinema was built in the south-west.
The two maps depict the infrastructural and commercial transformations that occurred in the coastal settlement of Pentland between 1950 and 2007.

Overall, Pentland experienced extensive modernization, transitioning from a predominantly rural, industrial site into a commercial and residential seaside town. The most prominent developments included the removal of industrial facilities and grasslands to make way for recreational venues, retail spaces, and housing developments.
In 1950, the town had a simple layout. A central thoroughfare stretched from the south to terminate at the shoreline in the north.
Branching off this road were two secondary lanes: one extended westward towards an industrial sector, while the other ran east to a circular car park.
The remaining territory on either side was entirely occupied by open grassland.
Over the 57-year period, the infrastructure was extensively upgraded.
A marine facility with yacht berths was introduced in the northern sea, accompanied by a semicircular coastal road hugging the shoreline.
The western industrial area converted into an amenity zone, featuring a park in the north-west, an adjoining swimming pool, and a multi-storey car park.
Meanwhile, the former eastern car park was cleared to construct apartment buildings.
In the southern half, the introduction of an east-west arterial road created a major intersection lined with retail shops.
Finally, the south-eastern area saw the construction of residential houses, while a cinema was erected opposite them in the south-west.
The maps illustrate a housing estate at present and the planned changes for its future development.

Overall, the housing estate will undergo major changes. Most of the trees will be cut down to make room for new sports, recreational amenities, and smaller houses, while the road network will be redesigned.
At present, a large curve private road connects to the main road in the north at two points.
Along this road, several four-bedroom houses are scattered around the area.
The whole estate is heavily covered by woodland, with a total of 6.000 trees.
In the future plan, only 250 woodland trees will remain in the northern area, while the rest will be cleared.
The private road will be changed: the northern loop will become smaller to surround the remaining trees, and a new straight road will run down to the south.
In the middle of the estate, a lake will be constructed in the west, while tennis courts will be built in the east.
Further south, a central flower garden will be added, surrounded by a loop of new one, two and three-bedroom houses.
Finally, three parkland areas will be introduced across the estate.
The maps illustrate the current layout of a residential area and the proposed redevelopment plan for its future.

Overall, the estate is set to be transformed from a sparsely populated, heavily wooded area into a modern, higher-density residential community. The vast majority of trees will be removed to facilitate new recreational infrastructure, recreational spaces, and diverse housing options.
Currently, the estate is characterized by dense woodland containing approximately 6,000 trees.
Access is provided by a curved private road that branches off the northern main road at two separate junctions, forming a broad loop.
A small number of detached four-bedroom houses are dispersed along both the interior and exterior sides of this route.
Under the proposed plan, deforestation will occur extensively, reducing the tree count drastically from 6,000 to just 250, concentrated entirely along the northern perimeter.
The road infrastructure will be modified into a smaller northern semi-circle connected to a central road running southward.
In the midsection, leisure amenities will be introduced, comprising an artificial lake to the west and tennis courts to the east.
The southern half will be dominated by a large communal flower garden encircled by modern one, two and three bedroom properties, completely replacing the precious four-bedroom dwellings.
In addition, three separate parkland areas will be interspersed between the recreational facilities and residential zones.
